discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators (the Z2 quantum spin Hall state)
subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases of matter)
motivation: Kane and Mele (2005) showed that time-reversal symmetry, together with spin-orbit coupling, permits a new insulating phase characterized by a Z2 topological invariant. It cannot be detected by any local order parameter, and it guarantees protected, helical edge states. Molenkamp's 2007 transport measurements on HgTe quantum wells confirmed this quantum spin Hall state through quantized edge conductance. The work soon extended to three-dimensional topological insulators. It turned topology from an occasional curiosity into an organizing principle for classifying band structures, and it gave rise to topological superconductors, Weyl semimetals, and topological photonic and mechanical metamaterials. Few ideas have so thoroughly reorganized how an entire community thinks: a homotopy invariant turned into counting edge modes in a real material. This is foundational physics of the highest order.
